html:
SMTO-ART-0004 — SMTO can't show a preview of this file

GUID: 6d95514a-5843-4176-987c-889eeee1364c
Slug: artifact-preview-unavailable
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't display this saved file inside the app. A failed preview does not establish that the file itself is damaged, and the Task's result hasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the preview window or the Artifacts from this run list, select Download, then open the file with a program on your computer. The preview is only a quick look; the download is the complete original file.
  2. Check whether the file shows a 🔒 Sensitive mark or a greyed-out View button. Sensitive files, very large files and some file types can only be downloaded. SMTO deliberately turns off previews for these files, so downloading is the expected way to open them.
  3. If Download also fails, read the error that Download shows and follow its steps instead. A failed preview alone says nothing about the file; a failed download points to the real problem.

What success looks like

  • The file downloads and opens normally on your computer, or the preview appears when you select View.

If it still fails

  • If both the preview and Download fail, select Copy error details in the error panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the file or the Task because the preview failed; the original may be fine.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The artifact preview or viewer endpoint refused or failed to render this artifact (preview disabled for sensitive, oversized or unsupported MIME types, or an ArtifactError while opening the verified stream); this does not establish that the original artifact is damaged.

What this means

  • Preview/viewer dispatch selects an unsupported/disabled presentation kind or catches an artifact error while rendering the view. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Preview/viewer dispatch selects an unsupported/disabled presentation kind or catches an artifact error while rendering the view.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect presentation kind and original artifact availability separately from preview failure.

How to fix it

  • Open or download the original artifact instead of the preview. Check the artifact's preview policy (mime_type, size_bytes, sensitive) from the artifact metadata endpoint: data previews support only csv, json and text, and the viewer only html and pdf within the byte ceilings in agent_runtime/artifacts/preview.py. Fetch the original through the artifact's download endpoint; if that also fails, diagnose the underlying ArtifactError (scope, deleted/quarantined or integrity) in the Server log instead of forcing a preview.
  • Download or open the original artifact through its supported action when available. Preserve preview diagnostics if rendering repeatedly fails.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported download/open accesses the original when available, or the actual artifact failure is diagnosed.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
